findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_tail.py` to the Scope section, since `_cancelled_plan_review_verdict` (a new function) is introduced there.
evidence: Scope lists: 'src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py, src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py, tests/unit/workflow/test_plan_review_cancel.py'
plan_review_tail.py:265 defines _cancelled_plan_review_verdict — a new function this ticket introduces
Context section acknowledges the file: 'the cancelled-verdict builder _cancelled_plan_review_verdict lives here' but Scope does not enumerate it

findings.finding: plan_review_tail.py is absent from the Scope section despite receiving new behavior (_cancelled_plan_review_verdict is a new function added to it in this ticket).
scenarios: A reviewer checking which files to inspect for this change would miss plan_review_tail.py and fail to review the new _cancelled_plan_review_verdict function.
Scope-based tooling or PR review filters that rely on the Scope list would not flag changes to plan_review_tail.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an Acceptance Criterion explicitly verifying the fail-open/monotone property: a fingerprint probe that returns None (read error or unavailable) must NOT cancel the review, and the run must proceed to the same sign-time behavior as today.
evidence: Approach (1): 'Returns True only when baseline and current are both non-None and differ; unknown/None → False (fail-open; monotone — a missed cancel degrades to today's sign-time refusal)'
Testing: 'monotone/fail-open: a probe whose fingerprint read returns None (read error) does not cancel; the run proceeds to sign-time behavior'
All five AC lines are enumerated; none covers the None-fingerprint / fail-open case
This is described as a deliberate design choice to avoid false cancels, making it an observable correctness property, not a mere implementation detail
findings.finding: The fail-open/monotone safety property — when `own_material_changed` returns None (fingerprint read error), the probe does NOT cancel and the run proceeds to sign-time behavior — is described in Approach (1) and tested in Testing ('monotone/fail-open' test case), but no Acceptance Criterion verifies this property. A safety-critical design invariant with no covering AC can be silently dropped or regressed without failing the acceptance gate.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (all five AC lines); Approach (1) paragraph on own_material_changed; Testing 'monotone/fail-open' bullet
scenarios: A refactor of own_material_changed that changes the None-handling (e.g., treats None as 'changed') would pass all five ACs while silently breaking the fail-open safety guarantee
During code review, the absence of an AC for this property makes it easy to argue the None-handling is 'gold-plating' and remove it
findings.suggested_fix: Add as AC-6: 'A fingerprint probe that returns None (e.g., due to a transient read error) does NOT cancel the review; the run proceeds and sign-time behavior is unchanged (checked: unit test asserting a None-returning current_material_fingerprint leaves the run completing normally, with the same verdict shape as an undisturbed run and no PlanReviewCancelledStale raised).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an ADR or AGENTS.md entry capturing: (a) the ContextVar+threading.Event cancel-scope pattern and why it was chosen over alternatives, (b) the two-seam placement rationale, and (c) the own-material-only scoping invariant and its d70a provenance, so future contributors can extend the cancel mechanism safely.
evidence: Plan text contains detailed design rationale for ContextVar selection, threading.Event, two-seam placement, and d70a own-material-only scoping, but Scope lists only src files and the new test file — no design doc update.

"Out of scope: the yaml (unchanged), the bespoke orchestrator (retired), verify-completion/code-review gates, any cancellation of in-flight runner calls" — no design-doc/ADR update mentioned anywhere in scope or acceptance criteria.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel architectural pattern — a ContextVar-based cancel scope with a shared threading.Event propagated into a thread-pool via copy_context(), scoped to own-material only to avoid the d70a regression — but specifies no update to any ADR, AGENTS.md, or design document. The rationale for the two-seam placement, the ContextVar+threading.Event choice (vs alternatives), and the own-material-only scoping rule are currently captured only in the plan/PR description, not in any persisted design artifact.
findings.location: Approach sections (1)–(4); Scope listing; no mention of ADR/AGENTS.md update
scenarios: A future engineer adding a third seam or a new gate type has no persisted record of why exactly two seams were chosen, why related_material drift was explicitly excluded, or why threading.Event was preferred; they must reconstruct intent from git blame or the PR body.
The d70a scoping constraint (own material only) is a non-obvious invariant; without a doc update it may be silently violated in a future probe addition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the plan's claim that the `_chunk` guard 'makes the funnel safe for any future seam': `_run_container` uses a separate pool calling `_timed_pairing` directly (not `_chunk`), so container criteria are not guarded — either extend the guard to `_timed_pairing` or narrow the claim to 'makes the single-turn and agent chunk paths safe'.
evidence: Plan step (3): 'it makes the funnel safe for any future seam at one Event-read of cost'
_run_container (pass1.py:176-327) calls _timed_pairing directly in its own ThreadPoolExecutor; _chunk is never on this call path
pass1.py:599-602: `_run_container` is invoked after the main pool, sharing the same cancellable run context but with no review_cancelled() guard in _timed_pairing
findings.finding: The plan's forward-looking safety claim that the `_chunk` guard 'makes the funnel safe for any future seam' is inaccurate: `_run_container` (pass1.py:176–327) uses a separate `ThreadPoolExecutor` calling `_timed_pairing` directly, completely bypassing `_chunk`. If a future seam were added that could set the cancel event before the container stage runs, `_run_container`'s pool would not be guarded. The plan presents this as full funnel safety, but the container fan-out is an uncovered execution path.
findings.location: Approach section, step (3) — `pass1._chunk` guard; pass1.py:479-490 vs pass1.py:176-327 (`_run_container`)
scenarios: A future developer adds a probe seam inside the batch step (or before the container stage) expecting the _chunk guard to cover container criteria — it does not; container LLM calls would proceed after cancellation
The plan's own safety rationale for the defensive guard is presented as complete, potentially misleading future implementers about the scope of coverage
findings.suggested_fix: In step (3), replace 'it makes the funnel safe for any future seam at one Event-read of cost' with 'it makes the single-turn and agent-chunk paths safe for any future seam; the container fan-out (_run_container/_timed_pairing) is a separate pool not covered by this guard'. Optionally add a `review_cancelled()` early-return at the top of `_timed_pairing` in the same story.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief 'why bespoke over prior art' note to the Approach §(1) rationale (or the code comment block at generation.py:68-79) acknowledging that Python cancellation-token libraries (cantok, cancel-contexts) and anyio.CancelScope exist but were not used because: (a) no async runtime is in scope, (b) the token must carry domain-specific own-material semantics, and (c) the `copy_context()` propagation idiom is already established in this codebase.
evidence: Plan names '_CancelScope dataclass {ticket_id, baseline_own_material, repo_root, event: threading.Event}' and 'cancel_scope(...) contextmanager' with no reference to prior-art alternatives.
Python PyPI hosts 'cantok' (ConditionToken/CounterToken/TimeoutToken) and 'cancel-contexts' (CancelContext / check_cancelled()) — direct analogues of this bespoke pattern.
anyio.CancelScope and trio.CancelScope are established Python precedents for the cancel-scope naming and context-manager shape the plan adopts.
ABSENCE: the plan contains no 'alternatives rejected' clause for the cancellation-token mechanism itself (only for the scoping predicate — tracker HEAD / relation snapshot).
findings.finding: The plan introduces a bespoke `_CancelScope + threading.Event` cooperative-cancellation mechanism without acknowledging the well-established Cancellation Token pattern (C#/.NET `CancellationToken`, Python `cantok`/`cancel-contexts` on PyPI, `anyio.CancelScope`) or briefly stating why bespoke was preferred over these prior-art options.
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer encountering `_CancelScope` with no prior-art rationale may not understand why a dependency was not preferred, and may reach for a library in a follow-on change that breaks the domain-specific own-material semantics.

If `cantok` or a similar library is already transitively present in the dependency graph, a future de-duplication pass may replace the bespoke token without understanding the ContextVar propagation and fail-open constraints.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the comment block at generation.py:68-79 with: '# Why not a library (cantok / anyio.CancelScope)? No async runtime is in scope; # the token must carry domain-specific fields (baseline fingerprint, repo_root, seam); # copy_context()-based ContextVar propagation is already the established idiom here.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete values for `seam` and `reason` in `coverage_extra["cancelled"]` — e.g. `seam` = the probe's op-function name string ('plan_review_verify_inputs' or 'plan_review_coach_inputs') and `reason` = a fixed literal like 'own_material_changed'.
evidence: Plan text: 'coverage_extra={"cancelled": {"seam": ..., "reason": ...}}' — the '...' are literal placeholders, not inferred values
No other plan section defines the seam or reason vocabulary
The Testing section checks 'the cancelled verdict shape' but does not specify what seam/reason values to assert
findings.finding: The `coverage_extra` dict in step (4) uses literal ellipsis placeholders for `seam` and `reason` (`{"seam": ..., "reason": ...}`) without specifying what values these fields should carry. An implementer must decide independently: possible choices for `seam` include the op function name ('plan_review_verify_inputs'/'plan_review_coach_inputs'), the yaml step name, or a generic enum; possible choices for `reason` include a fixed string like 'own_material_changed' or the result of `str(baseline) + ' -> ' + str(current)`. Nothing in the plan or the referenced source anchors these values.
scenarios: Two implementers independently choose different string values for seam/reason, producing divergent coverage_extra shapes that break downstream consumers parsing the cancelled verdict
A test author asserts a specific seam string that doesn't match what the implementer chose, causing a spurious test failure
findings.suggested_fix: In step (4), replace the ellipses with explicit values: `coverage_extra={"cancelled": {"seam": <probe_op_name: str>, "reason": "own_material_changed"}}` where `<probe_op_name>` is the string name of the calling op ('plan_review_verify_inputs' or 'plan_review_coach_inputs'). Update the Testing section to assert these exact values in the cancelled verdict shape check.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add at least one observable signal (e.g., a structured log line at WARNING level or a metrics counter increment) inside `probe_cancel` (or immediately after `scope.event.is_set()` is confirmed in `produce_plan_review_verdict`) so that mid-review cancel events are visible to operators without requiring raw verdict inspection.
evidence: The plan specifies `coverage_extra={\"cancelled\": {\"seam\": ..., \"reason\": ...}}` and `signature_reason=\"cancelled-stale\"` but names no log call, metric counter, or trace span.
ABSENCE: No section of the plan mentions instrumentation (log.warning, metrics.increment, structlog, OpenTelemetry, or equivalent) at the point the cancel fires.
The existing plan-review suite already emits sidecar events for normal verdicts; the cancel path explicitly skips sidecar.emit, leaving zero operational signal.
findings.finding: No logging, metric, or trace is specified for the cancel event firing. The cancel is recorded only in the verdict's `coverage_extra` and `finding id`, which are invisible to operators unless they inspect raw verdict structures. There is no way to alert on or aggregate mid-review cancel frequency, nor to debug whether false-cancels are occurring in production.
findings.location: Approach § (4) produce_plan_review_verdict; Approach § probe_cancel; Acceptance Criteria (all bullet points)
scenarios: A bug causes spurious cancels (e.g., fingerprint read returns stale data transiently) — operators see only a stream of exit-2 results with no aggregatable signal.
A deploy introduces a regression in `own_material_changed` — the absence of a counter or log makes it impossible to alert on increased cancel rates.
findings.suggested_fix: In `probe_cancel`, after `event.set()`, emit a structured log line: `logger.warning('plan_review_cancelled_stale', ticket_id=scope.ticket_id, seam=seam)`. In `produce_plan_review_verdict`, after confirming `scope.event.is_set()`, increment a counter such as `metrics.increment('plan_review.cancelled_stale', tags={'seam': ...})`. Both are one-liners and add no new dependencies.

findings.finding: plan_review_tail.py is an unenumerated edit target: the plan's Scope section lists gate_dispatch.py as the home of the cancelled-verdict builder and names only six files, but the implementation places _cancelled_plan_review_verdict in src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_tail.py (a separate leaf module that gate_dispatch re-imports). Step (4) explicitly says the cancelled verdict is 'built with claimability.indeterminate_verdict' in the gate_dispatch context, yet the actual creation site is plan_review_tail.py. An implementer following the plan spec would edit gate_dispatch.py directly, miss the module boundary, and either duplicate the function or break the re-import contract.
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, append `src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_tail.py`. In Step (4), change 'return a cancelled verdict built with ...' to 'add `_cancelled_plan_review_verdict(ctx, cfg, *, scope)` to `plan_review_tail.py` (the established leaf for plan-review failure-tail builders), imported and re-exported from `gate_dispatch.py` alongside the existing `_degraded_plan_review_verdict`'.
